title: Cross-language release sanity harness for streaming SDKs and retry ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add an automated, language-agnostic release sanity harness that validates SDK releases (Python, TypeScript, Go) for: 1) streaming ergonomics (server->client streaming points, reconnect behavior), 2) client-side retry semantics (idempotency keys, exponential backoff hooks), 3) packaging and publish workflows (PyPI, npm, go modules), and 4) provenance/signing verification (Sigstore/cosign attestations and checksums). The harness should run as part of the release CI pipeline and as a lightweight pre-release runner users can run locally. Deliverables: - e2e test matrix for each language covering streaming, retry, and partial-restore of in-flight streams - CI job templates for PyPI/npm/go publish verification that assert signature/attestation presence and checksum matches - lightweight CLI tool (validate-sdk-release) that downloads published artifact, verifies signature, runs a small streaming+retry scenario against a test endpoint, and emits a reproducible log for audits - docs + example workflows in /docs/release-harness.md Acceptance criteria: - CI gate fails if published artifacts lack a valid Sigstore attestation or checksum mismatch - streaming test covers mid-stream reconnect and KV cache warmup for each language's SDK example -> pass/fail deterministic - retry tests verify both idempotent and non-idempotent flows and assert no duplicate side effects in the mock service - validate-sdk-release CLI available in repo, integration tested in a release dry-run

acceptance_criteria: CI gate rejects release if signature/attestation missing or invalid
validate-sdk-release CLI verifies and runs streaming+retry scenarios with deterministic pass/fail
Language adapters (python, ts, go) implemented and exercised by e2e tests
Documentation with example commands for maintainers and auditors
Audit log produced by CI with artifact hash, attestation subject, and test result summary
implementation_notes: Language adapters will share a common harness interface (shell commands + JSON exchange) to avoid nested code dependencies between SDKs
Use a local mock test endpoint (docker-compose) that implements idempotency checks and stream reconnect behavior for deterministic tests
Prefer Sigstore/cosign for attestation format; store expected attestation subjects in repo under /release/expected_attestations.json
For Go modules, use a CI step to set GOPROXY and GOPRIVATE appropriately; publish via 'goreleaser' or 'go publish' with cosign signing
Keep validate-sdk-release CLI in repo as a small python tool to maximize contributor familiarity; it will shell out to language-specific test runners when needed
